title: Stream Harmony Reservoir and Attention Redistributor
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We observe sporadic 95th/99th tail spikes under mixed small/large sequence workloads caused by uneven admission during continuous batching and suboptimal kernel paths chosen for attention-heavy requests.

Goal: Reduce 95th and 99th token-latency by 20-30% for mixed workloads while keeping median latency within 5% of current. Deliver a runtime component that: (1) performs stream-aware admission shaping to limit cross-traffic noise, (2) surfaces attention-hint metadata to the kernel selector and scheduler, and (3) schedules prefill and decode windows to reduce KV-cache churn.

Design summary: Introduce a memory-and-latency aware reservoir (Stream Harmony Reservoir) that throttles admission per-stream based on three signals: active KV footprint, recent kernel runtime variance, and outstanding slot countdown. Admission decisions combine an 8-bit compact hint (attention-hot / attention-cold) and a micro-priority score that decays with time. Kernel selector will be extended with an attention-cost multiplier that prefers tall-narrow attention kernels for attention-hot streams and fused attention kernels for dense batches. Prefill/decode scheduling will attempt to colocate compatible prefill windows to reuse KV caches and bias scheduling to decode lanes with compatible kernel affinities.

Acceptance criteria (must be measurable):
- 95th token latency reduced by >=20% on the mixed-seq benchmark (mix: 40% short, 40% med, 20% long)
- 99th token latency reduced by >=15%
- Median latency regresses by <5%
- No increased OOMs or TLB thrash in stress tests
- Feature gated behind runtime flag `stream_harmony_v1`

Implementation notes:
- Admission controller: implement as a lightweight C++ component in runtime admission path with per-stream reservoir counters; fallback to fair-queue admission when flags disabled.
- Kernel hints: extend existing kernel descriptor with `attention_profile` (enum: NONE, SPARSE, DENSE, BLOCKED) serialized to request metadata. Kernel selection policy will compute score = base_latency_est + attention_profile_weight * attention_multiplier.
- Prefill scheduling: implement a window collator that groups prefill ops within 40ms windows when KV-compatible and pinned to the same GPU shard.
- Telemetry: emit new metrics `sh_reservoir_admit_rate`, `sh_kernel_affinity_misses`, `sh_prefill_colocations` and tag by model, region, and stream_type.

Trade-offs and risks:
- More aggressive colocation reduces cache misses but may increase head-of-line blocking for very short queries. We'll mitigate with time-limited colocation and a short-circuit for sub-50-token prefill lanes.
- Kernel selection based on hints requires accurate hinting from higher layers; if hints are noisy we may degrade throughput—we will add a noise-detection monitor and revert weights automatically.
- Complexity: adds cross-cutting changes (admission, selector, scheduler). We'll gate via feature flag and do canary rollout with per-model SLO guards.

Related artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Stream+Harmony+Reservoir+Design
- Spike PR (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4289
- Microbenchmark dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/bench/stream-reservoir-v1

comments: 2025-01-11 - Maya Chen: Kickoff sync completed. Agreed to scope initial prototype to admission + telemetry only. Action: Maya to land minimal admit counters by 2025-01-20.

2025-01-16 - Liam O'Connor: Spike shows 12% 95th improvement when we bias kernel selector with perfect attention hints (simulated). Link to notebook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/stream-hint-experiments

2025-01-21 - Maya Chen: Landed proto counters in runtime (PR: 4289). Telemetry emitted but we saw increased 50th latency for tiny (<20 token) requests when reservoir threshold low. Added short-circuit bypass for short queries; test coverage added. PR review by Arjun and Priya.

2025-01-25 - Arjun Patel: Reviewed kernel-selector changes. Suggest using exponential backoff rather than linear decay for micro-priority to reduce oscillation when streams go bursty. Also raised concern about serializing attention_profile in hot path—suggest packing into 8-bit header.

2025-01-28 - Liam O'Connor: Implemented packed 8-bit attention hint and exp-decay for micro-priority. Benchmarks: end-to-end mixed-seq 95th improved 22%, 99th improved 12% on dev cluster (gpu-x1-large). See benchmark run: https://bench.redwood.ai/runs/2025-01-28-582407

2025-02-03 - QA (Priya Rao): Integration tests pass on fare workloads. Noted one regression: a model with heavy KV state (conversation model) had minor increase in GPU memory churn when prefill collator colocated windows aggressively. Lowered colocation window from 60ms to 40ms and re-ran tests.

2025-02-09 - SRE (Diego Morales): Canary in us-west-2 shows stable CPU usage; reservoir admit_rate is stable. Observed a rare path where kernel_affinity_misses spike under multi-tenant bursts (0.03% of requests). Diego created follow-up ENG-583999 to add affinity warmup heuristics.

2025-02-12 - Maya Chen: Ramp plan approved. Feature flag `stream_harmony_v1` will be enabled for 10% traffic for next 2 weeks with automatic rollback on SLO regressions. Next: finalize rollout runbook and postmortem template.
